sentence: It's about twelve thousand seven hundred kilometers.
claim: A tunnel through Earth's centre is one diameter long: 2 × 6,371 km = 12,742 km, said as about 12,700 km.
note: Volumetric mean radius 6,371.000 km (fact sheet, bulk parameters). Computed in calc.py: diameter_m = 12742000 m, rounded to 3 figures.

sentence: Driving it nonstop at highway speed takes about five days.
claim: At 100 km/h without stopping, 12,742 km takes about 127 hours: about 5 days.
note: Computed in calc.py (drive_h = 127.4 h = 5.31 days) from the radius above and an assumed highway speed of 100 km/h, a round figure; at 110 km/h it is 4.8 days, at 90 km/h 5.9: 'about five days' holds for 100 ± 10 km/h.

sentence: By the center: about ten kilometers a second.
claim: Falling from rest at the surface with no air, the speed at Earth's centre is about 10 km/s (PREM density: 9.92 km/s; a uniform Earth gives 7.91 km/s).
source_title: A. M. Dziewonski & D. L. Anderson, "Preliminary reference Earth model", Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 25, 297–356 (1981)
note: Computed in calc.py: v^2 = 2 × integral of g(r) from the centre to the surface, g(r) = G·M(<r)/r^2 with PREM's density polynomials (table 1 of the paper). Klotz (2015) gives the same physics; his paper is the cross-check.

sentence: Then it slows you, and you reach the far side just as you stop.
claim: In the idealised tunnel (no air or friction, no rotation) the faller decelerates past the centre and comes to rest exactly at the far surface: energy is conserved and the potential is symmetric.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: The paper's model is frictionless and treats the trip as an oscillation through the centre; the badges on screen say 'no air', 'no heat', 'no spin'.

sentence: The textbook answer was forty-two minutes.
claim: The classic textbook answer for a fall through a uniform-density Earth is about 42 minutes (42 min 12 s), from P. W. Cooper, Am. J. Phys. 34, 68 (1966).
source_title: How Long Would It Take to Fall Through the Earth? (Live Science, 2015)
note: Excerpt: Cooper's 1966 paper in the American Journal of Physics showed a tube along the diameter would take 42 minutes; Klotz quotes 42 min 12 s. calc.py: pi·sqrt(R^3/GM) = 2530 s = 42.17 min.

sentence: It assumed Earth is equally dense all the way down.
claim: The 42-minute result assumes Earth's density is the same at every depth.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: Excerpt: Klotz used seismic-based Earth structure instead of assuming uniform density. 'Equally dense all the way down' is the uniform-density assumption in plain words.

sentence: Then a graduate student, Alexander Klotz, used the real Earth.
claim: Alexander Klotz, then a McGill University graduate student, recomputed the fall using Earth's real density profile, from seismic data (PREM); the 'PREM density (seismology)' badge is on screen as this is said.
source_title: How Long Would It Take to Fall Through the Earth? (Live Science, 2015)
note: Excerpt: a McGill University grad student; seismic-based density data. Also KL (the paper).

sentence: The core is so dense that gravity gets stronger before it fades.
claim: With PREM's density, gravity inside the tunnel rises from 9.8 m/s^2 at the surface to a maximum of about 10.7 m/s^2 at the core–mantle boundary (3480 km from the centre), then falls to zero at the centre; Earth's core averages about 2.5 times the density of the mantle and crust above it.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: Computed in calc.py (g_max, r_gmax_km, rho_core_mean 10987 kg/m^3 vs rho_crust_mantle_mean 4449 kg/m^3). Klotz's paper shows the same rise of g through the mantle (that is why constant g is a good approximation).

claim: With the real (PREM) density, the fall through the centre takes about 38 minutes: 38 min 11 s in the paper; calc.py gets 2291 s = 38.18 min.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: Excerpt: Solving the problem numerically, Klotz found that an object should fall through Earth in 38 minutes and 11 seconds. calc.py reproduces it to within a second, which also checks the density table (its mass comes out within 0.02% of NASA's).

sentence: With nothing to stop you, you'd fall back and forth, a round trip every seventy-six minutes, forever.
claim: Without friction the fall repeats: there and back takes twice the one-way time, 2 × 38.2 min ≈ 76 minutes.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: Computed: 2 × t_prem = 76.4 min, said as seventy-six. 'Forever' holds only in the idealised, frictionless tunnel (badged).

sentence: Make the core ten percent lighter: about thirty-nine.
claim: Sensitivity: with the core's density 10% lower (mantle unchanged), the fall takes about 39 minutes (39.2 min); 10% higher, about 37 (37.3 min).
source_title: A. M. Dziewonski & D. L. Anderson, "Preliminary reference Earth model", Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 25, 297–356 (1981)
note: Computed in calc.py by scaling PREM's core polynomials; a sensitivity check, not a claim about the real core (PREM's core density is known far better than ±10%).

claim: With a uniform-density Earth, the fall takes about 42 minutes.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: The paper's uniform case (42 min 12 s); calc.py 42.17 min.

sentence: They're the pull of Earth's heavy core.
claim: The difference between the uniform and real-Earth answers is about 4 minutes (4.0 min), and it comes from mass concentrated toward the centre: the core is about 16% of Earth's volume but about 32% of its mass.
source_title: A. R. Klotz, "The gravity tunnel in a non-uniform Earth", Am. J. Phys. 83, 231 (2015); arXiv:1308.1342
note: Computed in calc.py (core_mass_frac, core_vol_frac). 'The pull of Earth's heavy core' is the plain-words version: with the mass spread evenly the trip would take the uniform 42 minutes.
